dedupe_keys.name: dsmlib regionalised load shifting potential tool with the region4flex example for germany

description: dsmlib is a Python tool that calculates regionalised load shifting (demand response) potentials and cost-potential curves. The Zenodo page says it is published with the input data and results of the region4FLEX example, which applies it to the 401 German NUTS-3 districts across residential, commercial, industrial, power-to-heat, power-to-gas and e-mobility demand, with industrial technologies such as air separation, cement production, pulping, paper and recycled paper production and process heat, and results such as average and maximum load increase potentials for 2030 in MW and MWh. It accompanies the 2020 Advances in Applied Energy paper by Heitkoetter, Schyska and Schmidt, and was published on 18 August 2020 as a quick-start archive of about 115 MB and a full archive of about 3.4 GB, downloadable, with the code under GPL v3, results under CC BY 4.0 and inputs under various open licences. Coverage is national for Germany at district level. Caveats: the page says time series and large inputs are only in the full download, and future updates are not stated on the page read. For simulation it gives district-level flexibility of industrial and other loads for power system models, useful to test how demand response at factories eases grid congestion or shortfalls. Related catalogue records include the VEA industrial load profiles, the SIELS industrial load shapes and the Benguerir mine hourly energy data.
name: dsmlib - regionalised load shifting potential tool with the region4FLEX example for Germany
